mainTopic: רב חסדא's rule that one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is פטור, and the challenges to it
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that חזה ושוק cannot apply to חולין, since waving them inside would bring חולין into the עזרה. So the word ״זֶה״ teaches רב חסדא's rule instead: one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is פטור from paying. The reason is either the word ״זֶה״ or that the gifts are ממון שאין לו תובעים, money no single כהן can claim. Two ברייתות that call the gifts 'דין' seem to challenge this. The גמרא explains that judges decide which כהנים get the gifts, since an עם הארץ gets none. It also explains that a כהן can sue only for gifts that already came into his hands, even before they were separated. A משנה about a traveling homeowner who takes gifts for the poor is answered as מדת חסידות, not a legal debt. A last ברייתא about eating טבל implies that after הרמה one must pay. The גמרא begins its answer with 'הכא נמי', and the rest of the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Waving inside would bring non-sacred animals into the Temple courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes showing that waving the חזה ושוק of a חולין animal is impossible, so no פסוק is needed to exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were waved inside the מקדש, he would be bringing חולין into the עזרה. So it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an argument that started just before this line. Waving the breast and thigh of a non-sacred animal cannot be done properly anywhere, so it can never happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of waving outside was already ruled out. Now the inside option is ruled out too, because bringing חולין into the עזרה is forbidden. Since the whole procedure is impossible for חולין, we do not need the word ״זֶה״ to tell us that חזה ושוק do not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: inside (here: inside the מקדש)
bringing non-sacred animals into the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
therefore
it is not possible

phrases.english: If inside —
phrases.notes: Inside the מקדש. Waving outside was just ruled out, so now the גמרא checks waving inside.

phrases.english: he is bringing non-sacred animals into the courtyard,
therefore it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַגַּוַּאי קָא מְעַיֵּיל חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an argument from the previous section of the daf
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that ״זֶה״ is needed to exclude חזה ושוק of חולין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The procedure is impossible for חולין anyway, so no verse is needed to exclude it

steps.title: So why does the verse say 'this'?
steps.stepSummary: Since ״זֶה״ is not needed for חזה ושוק, the גמרא asks what the word is teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need the word ״זֶה״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It asks what the word ״זֶה״ is for, now that its first use has been ruled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no word in the תורה is extra. Once the previous step showed ״זֶה״ is not needed to exclude חזה ושוק, the word must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (asking what a word or rule adds)
'this': the word in the פסוק about the priests' gifts

phrases.english: But why do I need “this”?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 1: since ״זֶה״ isn't needed there, what is it for?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word ״זֶה״ in the פסוק teaches

steps.title: The word teaches רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: ״זֶה״ teaches רב חסדא's rule: someone who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is פטור from paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רב חסדא's rule. רב חסדא said: one who damages the priestly gifts, or eats them, is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״זֶה״ is the source for רב חסדא's teaching about damaging the priestly gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זֶה״ means 'this very thing'. The כהן gets these actual parts of the animal, not money in their place. So if the parts are destroyed or eaten, there is no payment.

keyTerms.meaning: priestly gifts: the foreleg, jaw and maw given to a כהן
one who causes damage
exempt from paying

phrases.english: For that of Rav Chisda,
as Rav Chisda said:
One who damages the gifts of the priesthood
or who ate them —
is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״זֶה״ teaches that one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה need not pay
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the topic of the rest of this section.

steps.title: רב חסדא's rule examined on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רב חסדא's statement in order to study it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main statement: רב חסדא said, one who damages the priestly gifts or eats them is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב חסדא's rule so it can examine it. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is now studying the statement itself, not just using it to explain the פסוק. That opens the door to asking for its reason.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': returning to examine a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Chisda said:
One who damages the gifts of the priesthood, or who ate them —
is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the statement quoted in step 3 in order to analyze it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is פטור from paying

steps.title: What is the reason for the exemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב חסדא's rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally someone who damages another person's property must pay. So we need to know why the priestly gifts are different.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the one who damages מתנות כהונה is פטור

steps.title: Two possible reasons
steps.stepSummary: Either the word ״זֶה״, or the gifts are ממון שאין לו תובעים, money that no one person can claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because ״זֶה״ is written. Or if you want, say it is because it is money that has no claimants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different possible reasons for רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one comes from the פסוק: only the actual parts are given, never a replacement. Reason two is logical: the owner may give the gifts to any כהן he chooses. So no single כהן can say 'you owe me', and with nobody to make a claim, nobody can collect.

keyTerms.meaning: if you wish, say (offering one of two possible answers)
money with no claimants: no specific person can demand it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the gifts are not real property of the כהנים. The point is only that no single כהן can claim them, so there is nobody to collect payment.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is because “this” is written,
and if you wish, say it is because it is
money that has no claimants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with two options
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the פסוק's word ״זֶה״, or the logic of ממון שאין לו תובעים

steps.title: A ברייתא calls the gifts a 'judgment'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the gifts are 'דין'. The גמרא suggests this means a כהן can collect them through the courts, which would mean they do have claimants.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: “And this shall be the priests' due (משפט)” teaches that the gifts are a judgment. For what law? Is it not that they can be taken out through judges?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second reason with a ברייתא that links the gifts to judges and courts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a court can force the owner to hand over the gifts, then the gifts do have someone who can claim them. That would go against the reason ממון שאין לו תובעים.

keyTerms.meaning: due or right; it can also mean judgment
a legal judgment, enforced by a court
for what law? (what practical difference)
to take them out of the owner's hands through judges

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
“And this shall be the priests' due” —
teaches that the gifts are a judgment.
For what law?
Is it not to extract them through judges?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second reason given in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason ממון שאין לו תובעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If courts can force the owner to give the gifts, then they have claimants, so the damager should have to pay

steps.title: Judges only decide how the gifts are divided
steps.stepSummary: The 'judgment' is about how the gifts are divided among כהנים, not about a כהן claiming them in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means they are divided through judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court tells the owner which kind of כהנים should receive the gifts. That does not make any single כהן a claimant, so the reason ממון שאין לו תובעים still works.

keyTerms.meaning: to divide them through judges: the court decides how the gifts are given out

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is פטור from paying. The reason is either the word ״זֶה״ or that they are ממון שאין לו תובעים. Calling the gifts 'דין' only means the court decides how they are divided.

phrases.english: No, it is to divide them through judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'דין' means a כהן can collect the gifts in court
steps.terutzMaskana: 'דין' means the court decides how the gifts are distributed; there is still no individual claimant

steps.title: Support: gifts are not given to a כהן who is an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its answer that judges decide which כהנים get the gifts. It cites רבי יונתן: we do not give gifts to a כהן who is an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what רב שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know not to give a gift to a כהן who is an עם הארץ? The פסוק says to give the portion to the כהנים 'so they may hold strong to the Torah of ה׳.' Whoever holds strong to the Torah gets a portion. Whoever does not, gets none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the idea of 'dividing the gifts through judges' comes from. Someone has to decide which כהנים deserve them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said 'דין' means the gifts are divided by judgment. Here we learn why a judgment is needed: only a כהן who keeps the Torah should get gifts. So a בית דין decides who qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person who is not careful with the Torah's laws
A portion or share
Someone who holds strong to the Torah, who learns it and keeps it

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the gifts have 'judgment' attached to them without saying any כהן can sue for them. That keeps רב חסדא's view safe.

phrases.english: And this is like Rav Shmuel bar Nachmani,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: as Rav Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
From where do we know that we do not give a gift
to a kohen who is an am ha'aretz?
As it says: "And he told the people, those living in Jerusalem,
to give the portion of the kohanim and the Levites,
so that they may hold strong to the Torah of ה׳"

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּחְזִיק בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ – יֵשׁ לוֹ מְנָת,
phrases.english: Whoever holds strong to the Torah of ה׳ has a portion,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מַחֲזִיק בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ – אֵין לוֹ מְנָת.
phrases.english: and whoever does not hold strong to the Torah of ה׳ has no portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for step 8's answer that 'judgment' means deciding how the gifts are divided.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the gifts are divided by judges, meaning judges decide which כהנים get them
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's reading of דברי הימים ב 31:4, which says gifts go only to a כהן who keeps the Torah

steps.title: A new ברייתא: only some gifts are called a judgment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. רבי יהודה בן בתירא learns from 'משפט' that the gifts are a 'דין', and from 'זה' that חזה ושוק are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: 'משפט' teaches that the gifts are a judgment. You might think that even חזה ושוק are a judgment. So the פסוק says 'זה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to test רב חסדא again. This step only quotes the source; the next steps will work out how it becomes a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a difference between the foreleg, jaw and maw, which are 'judgment', and חזה ושוק (the breast and thigh from קדשים), which are not. The גמרא will ask what that difference could mean.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Due' or 'judgment', the word in the פסוק about the כהן's gifts
The breast and thigh given to the כהן from שלמים offerings
'You might think', which sets up an idea the פסוק will reject
'The פסוק teaches', which brings the word that proves the point

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
"Due (mishpat)" teaches that the gifts are a judgment.
phrases.notes: From דברים 18:3: "And this shall be the כהנים' due."

phrases.english: You might think that even the breast and thigh are a judgment?
So the verse says "This."
phrases.notes: 'This' means only these gifts, the foreleg, jaw and maw, and not the breast and thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new test of רב חסדא's ruling with a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the gifts are ממון שאין לו תובעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only these gifts are 'judgment', the difference may be that a כהן can claim them in court. That would mean they do have claimants.

steps.title: What does 'judgment' mean here? Not division
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'judgment' means in this ברייתא. It rejects 'dividing through judges', because חזה ושוק are also divided through judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it a judgment? If you say it means dividing them through judges, are חזה ושוק not divided through judges too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to explain the word 'דין' in the ברייתא. It finds that the step 8 explanation (division) does not work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says חזה ושוק are NOT 'judgment'. But חזה ושוק are also a 'מנת', a portion, so they too go only to worthy כהנים through judges. So 'judgment' here must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what?', meaning what is this law about
To divide it among כהנים through judges
'Is that to say…?', a question asking whether something is really so

phrases.english: For what [is it a judgment]?
If you say: to divide it through judges,
is that to say that the breast and thigh
are not divided through judges?
phrases.notes: They are also a 'portion' from the פסוק in step 9, so judges divide them too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the ברייתא from step 10 and rules out the 'division' explanation using step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'דין' means in a ברייתא that excludes חזה ושוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not division through judges, since חזה ושוק are divided that way too

steps.title: So 'judgment' must mean taking the gifts through court
steps.stepSummary: The only meaning left is that a כהן can take the gifts from the owner through judges. That goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean taking them out through judges?
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is now complete. If a כהן can get the gifts through court, they have someone who can claim them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the owner who ate the gifts is exempt because no one can claim them. If this ברייתא lets a כהן force the owner in court, then רב חסדא's reason falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, isn't it…?', which brings the only explanation left
To take it out of the owner's hands through judges

phrases.english: Rather, is it not to take it out [from the owner] through judges?
phrases.notes: Some versions say להוציא, in round brackets. The word in square brackets, להוציאו ('to take it out'), is the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that began in step 10, now that 'division' has been ruled out.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's exemption, based on ממון שאין לו תובעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן who can sue for the gifts is a claimant, so the gifts are not money without claimants.

steps.title: The gifts were already in the כהן's hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about gifts that already came into the כהן's possession and were then taken from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where the gifts already came into his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. The ברייתא's court case is about gifts that already belonged to a specific כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a particular כהן owns the gifts, taking them from him is plain theft, and he can sue. That does not mean an owner who never gave the gifts can be sued, so רב חסדא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here, what case are we dealing with?', which narrows a source to a specific case
They came into his hand, meaning he already owns them

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where they came into his hand.
phrases.notes: The כהן already had the gifts, and then the owner took them back from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12 by limiting the ברייתא to a narrow case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets any כהן sue the owner for gifts the owner never gave.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means a כהן can sue for gifts that already belonged to him.

steps.title: Then why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the gifts already belong to the כהן, of course he can get them back in court. Why would the ברייתא need to teach that?
steps.simpleTranslation: If they came into his hands, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. It seems too obvious for the ברייתא to bother teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can sue to get back his own stolen property. If the ברייתא only teaches that, it would be saying nothing new. So the answer needs to be sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is there to say?', meaning that is obvious

phrases.english: If they came into his hand,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 13 as making the ברייתא pointless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about gifts already in the כהן's hands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person can always sue for his own stolen property, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: Gifts not yet separated count as separated
steps.stepSummary: The כהן got the whole animal before the gifts were separated out. This תנא holds that gifts not yet separated count as if they were separated, so the כהן already owns them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is that the animal came into his hands while the gifts were still not separated. This תנא holds that gifts not yet separated are treated as if they were separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its answer, which ends the challenge. The new point is that the כהן owns the gifts even before anyone has cut them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the gifts were never set apart, you might think they do not yet belong to the כהן. The ברייתא teaches that they already count as his, so the owner who takes them is stealing and the כהן can sue. רב חסדא's case, gifts never given to any כהן, is untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: Still 'untithed', meaning the gifts were not yet separated from the animal
A sage of the משנה period, here the author of the ברייתא

keyTerms.term: מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמוּ כְּמִי שֶׁהוּרְמוּ דָּמְיָין
keyTerms.meaning: Gifts not yet separated are treated as if they were already separated

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא survives. The 'judgment' in the ברייתא lets a כהן sue only for gifts that are already his. They count as his even before they are separated.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בטבליהו' does not mean the gifts are real טבל of produce. It is borrowed language: the animal is like untithed food, because the gifts have not been taken out yet.

phrases.english: Where they came into his hand while still "untithed,"
phrases.notes: The כהן got the whole animal before the gifts were cut out of it.

phrases.english: and this tanna holds:
gifts that have not been separated
are considered as if they were separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲתוֹ לִידֵיהּ בְּטִבְלַיְיהוּ, וְקָסָבַר הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by adding a new legal point that makes the ברייתא worth teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sharpening the case and adding a legal principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gifts still attached to the animal are not yet the כהן's, so he could not sue for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gifts not yet separated already count as the כהן's, so he can sue. רב חסדא is not contradicted.

steps.title: The traveling homeowner who takes gifts for the poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a homeowner traveling away from home may take gifts for the poor, but רבי אליעזר says he must pay them back later. This seems to challenge רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A homeowner who was traveling from place to place and needed to take לקט, שכחה, פאה, or מעשר עני may take them, and when he gets home he must pay. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge רב חסדא. The משנה says a homeowner who took gifts meant for the poor must pay for them later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No poor person ever owned these gifts before the homeowner took them, yet רבי אליעזר still requires him to pay. That looks like gifts that were never in anyone's hands can still be claimed back. רב חסדא holds that someone who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is exempt, so this משנה seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest, left for the poor
Forgotten sheaves, left for the poor
The corner of the field, left for the poor
The poor man's tithe
A homeowner (here, a man who is not poor)

steps.confusionAlert: This homeowner is wealthy at home. He only needs the gifts because he is stuck on the road without money. That is why there is any question of paying back.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A homeowner who was passing
from place to place,
and needs to take gleanings, forgotten sheaves,
pe'ah, or the poor man's tithe, he may take them,
and when he returns home he will pay,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵר מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about 'judgment' was answered, the גמרא brings a new source against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that one who damages or eats gifts that no one has taken yet does not pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר requires payment for poor gifts that never reached any poor person. So gifts that were not yet received can be claimed.

steps.title: Paying back is only an act of piety
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה's 'he will pay' is only מדת חסידות, not a legal obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Here they taught a rule of extra piety.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends himself. He says the משנה only means a pious person should pay. The law does not force him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the strict law, no poor person can force the homeowner to pay, which fits רב חסדא's view. The משנה is just teaching the right thing for a good person to do.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule of piety: going beyond what the law requires

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
They taught a rule of piety here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the obligation as a matter of piety, not law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He will pay' means a real legal debt the poor can collect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying is only the pious thing to do. Legally he is exempt.

steps.title: רבא: The משנה clearly says 'he will pay'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב חסדא's answer, because the משנה uses the plain word 'ישלם', which sounds like a real obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The תנא says 'he will pay', and you say it is only a rule of piety?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב חסדא's answer. The word 'ישלם' is too strong to mean just a nice extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An explicit 'he will pay' sounds like a legal duty. Reading it as mere piety twists the plain words of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He will pay

phrases.english: Rava said:
The tanna teaches "he will pay,"
and you say
that they taught a rule of piety here?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב חסדא's 'piety' reading of רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The explicit word 'ישלם' cannot easily mean only piety.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is not a good base for a challenge
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that one should not challenge רב חסדא from רבי אליעזר in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, should someone get up and challenge from רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now goes after the challenge itself. He says רבי אליעזר's opinion is not a strong enough source to attack רב חסדא with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's view is argued on by the חכמים in the same משנה, so רב חסדא can simply hold like the חכמים. This sets up the next step, where the challenge moves to the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: adding a second point
Get up and raise a challenge

phrases.english: And furthermore,
should one get up and challenge from Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: The חכמים argue with him right in the same משנה, so his view is weak ground for an attack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second point by רבא, this time against the challenge of step 16 itself.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge from רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is built on a view the חכמים reject.

steps.title: The challenge moves to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the חכמים instead. They exempt the traveler only because he was poor at the time, which implies a rich man would pay. Why, if damaging gifts that were not yet given is exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, challenge from the end of the משנה: the חכמים say he was a poor man at that time. The reason is that he was poor, but a rich man would pay. Why? It should be like someone who damages or eats מתנות כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a better challenge from the second half of the משנה. It reads the חכמים as implying that a rich man who took poor gifts must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים exempt the traveler only because on the road he counted as poor. So a man who really was rich would have to pay. But רב חסדא says one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is exempt, so a rich man here should also be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
The reason: introduces an inference from the stated reason
But: this would mean that...
One who damages the gifts owed to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים never say 'a rich man pays'. The גמרא is drawing that from their reason, 'he was poor at that time'.

phrases.english: Rather, challenge from the latter clause:
And the Rabbis say:
he was a poor man at that time,
the reason is that he was poor,
but a rich man would pay.
Why?
Let it be like one who damages gifts of the priesthood
or eats them!
phrases.notes: רב חסדא ruled earlier that such a person does not have to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected challenge from רבי אליעזר with one from the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's exemption for one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From the חכמים we infer that a rich man must pay for poor gifts he took, even though no poor person ever held them. That contradicts רב חסדא's exemption.

steps.title: Again: only an act of piety
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the implied payment by a rich man is only מדת חסידות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Here they taught a rule of piety.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the same answer as before, this time for the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer works better. The חכמים never wrote 'he will pay'. That was only inferred, so it can mean a pious extra and not a legal duty. רב חסדא's rule stands: no one can force payment for gifts that were never received.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught
Pays

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's view survives. Gifts that never reached the poor or the כהן cannot be claimed in court. Any 'payment' implied in the משנה is only מדת חסידות.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
They taught a rule of piety here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מִדַּת חֲסִידוּת שָׁנוּ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the implied obligation as piety
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rich man who took poor gifts owes a legal debt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Legally he is exempt. Paying is only the pious thing to do.

steps.title: A ברייתא: eating untithed produce is exempt from payment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בעל הבית or לוי who ate produce while it was still טבל does not pay, because the כהן has rights only from the time of הרמה onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: How do we know that a homeowner who ate his produce while it was still untithed, or a לוי who ate his tithes while they were still untithed, is exempt from paying? The פסוק says: 'And they shall not profane the holy things of בני ישראל which they set apart.' You have a claim on them only from the time they are set apart and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in order to set up a new challenge against רב חסדא. This step only presents the source. The challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before תרומה is separated, no specific part of the produce belongs to the כהן yet, so eating it costs the כהן nothing he can claim. The פסוק 'אשר ירימו' ties the כהן's rights to the moment of הרמה. The גמרא will use this exact time limit to build its question.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Tithes. Here it means the מעשר that a לוי receives, from which he must still separate תרומת מעשר
Payment, here meaning compensation owed to the כהן
The act of separating תרומה from the produce

phrases.english: Come and hear:
From where do we know, regarding a homeowner
who ate his produce while it was untithed,
and likewise a לוי who ate his tithes while they were untithed,
from where do we know that he is exempt from payment?
The verse teaches:
'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel
which they set apart'.
You (the כהן) have no claim on them
except from the time of separation and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִנַּיִן לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁאָכַל פֵּירוֹתָיו טְבָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב חסדא survived the challenges from רבי אליעזר and the חכמים, the גמרא brings a new source to test his view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who eats produce while it is טבל is exempt from paying the כהן, because the כהן's rights begin only at הרמה.

steps.title: After separation he pays, which contradicts רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that after הרמה the eater must pay, and asks why, since according to רב חסדא damaging or eating מתנות כהונה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that from the time of separation onward, at least, he does pay. Why? Let it be like someone who damages מתנות כהונה or eats them, who is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא from the other side and uses it to challenge רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the exemption to before הרמה. That suggests that after הרמה the eater must pay. But once תרומה is separated, it is a regular case of מתנות כהונה, and רב חסדא says one who damages or eats those is exempt. So the ברייתא seems to argue against him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'At least' or 'in any case'. It marks the part of the inference the גמרא is sure of
'Why?', an opening that challenges a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two times. Before הרמה the ברייתא says he is exempt, and everyone agrees with that. The question is only about the implied case after הרמה, where the ברייתא suggests he pays and רב חסדא would say he doesn't.

phrases.english: This implies that from the time of separation onward
at least, he pays.
Why?
Let it be like one who damages gifts of the priesthood
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא's ruling from earlier, that such a person is exempt.

phrases.english: or eats them!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִשְּׁעַת הֲרָמָה וְאֵילָךְ מִיהָא מְשַׁלֵּם, אַמַּאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied ruling from the ברייתא in step 22 and turns it against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is exempt from paying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא exempts only before הרמה, which implies that after הרמה one pays. That contradicts רב חסדא's exemption for מתנות כהונה.

steps.title: The answer begins: here too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer for רב חסדא with 'הכא נמי', and the rest of the answer continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to defend רב חסדא. Only the opening words appear here, and the full answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכא נמי' tells us the גמרא will explain this case the same way it explained an earlier case, so that רב חסדא's rule still holds. The details of how it does this come in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here too'. It signals that the same explanation used before applies to this case as well

phrases.english: Here too

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the response to the challenge raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Begins an answer that applies the same reasoning used before to this case. The full answer continues in the next section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies that one must pay after הרמה, which contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is still in progress. It will explain why this case does not contradict רב חסדא.
